Rashi on Shabbat 31a:10:1.english: The order of Zera’im - For [one] relies on a person’s faithfulness to separate his tithes properly.

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:10:2.hebrew: חוסן - לשון יורשין, ועל ידי אשה נולדו יורשין:
Rashi on Shabbat 31a:10:2.english: Strength - An expression of heirs; and through a woman, heirs are born.

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:10:3.hebrew: סדר נזיקין - מושיען, מזהיר לפרוש מהיזק ומהתחייב ממון:
Rashi on Shabbat 31a:10:3.english: The order of Nezikin - [It] saves them, [as it] warns [one] to refrain from [causing] damage and from incurring monetary liability.

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:10:5.english: It is His treasure - It is the primary thing that is valuable in His eyes to store up and make into a treasured possession for remembrance.

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:11:1.hebrew: קבעת עתים - לפי שאדם צריך להתעסק בדרך ארץ — שאם אין דרך ארץ אין תורה — הוצרך לקבוע עתים לתורה, דבר קצוב, שלא ימשך כל היום לדרך ארץ:
Rashi on Shabbat 31a:11:1.english: Did you designate times - Since a person must engage in worldly occupation — for “if there is no worldly occupation, there is no Torah” — he needed to designate fixed times for Torah, a set amount, so that he would not be drawn into worldly occupation all day.

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:11:2.english: In procreation - That is [the word] ḥosen [in the verse].

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:11:3.english: Did you await salvation - For the words of the prophets [to be fulfilled].

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:11:4.english: Did you understand one matter from another - This is “knowledge” [in the verse].

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:11:5.hebrew: קב חומטין - ארץ מלחה, ומשמרת את הפירות מהתליע:
Rashi on Shabbat 31a:11:5.english: A kav of ḥomtin - Salty earth, which preserves the produce from becoming wormy.

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:12:1.hebrew: ואינו חושש - למוכרה בדמי חטין, דלאו אונאה היא, שהרי שמירתן בכך:
Rashi on Shabbat 31a:12:1.english: And need not be concerned - [About] selling it at the price of wheat, for it is not fraud, as their preservation is [achieved] through this.

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:1:1.hebrew: שהמרו - נתערבו, כמו שממרין את היונים דסנהדרין (דף כו:):
Rashi on Shabbat 31a:1:1.english: Who wagered - They made a wager, as in "who race pigeons" in Sanhedrin (daf 26b).

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:1:2.hebrew: מי כאן הלל - כלום כאן הלל, ולשון גנאי לנשיא ישראל:
Rashi on Shabbat 31a:1:2.english: Who here is Hillel - [Meaning,] is Hillel here? And [it was] a derogatory expression toward the Nasi of Israel.

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:1:3.hebrew: מפני מה ראשן של בבליים סגלגלות - בילונ"ה בלעז, שאינו עגול. לישנא אחרינא: ראשן של בבליים סגלגל — עגול:
Rashi on Shabbat 31a:1:3.english: Why are the heads of Babylonians oval? - Beslonge in Old French, which is not round. Another version: The heads of Babylonians are segalgal — [meaning] round.

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:2:2.hebrew: שדרים בין החולות - והרוח נושבת ונכנס בתוך עיניהם. ובמקום אחר מפרש: "תרוטות" — לשון עגולות בית מושב שלהן. ואף כאן אני אומר כן, ומפני שדרים בין החולות שינה אותם המקום, שלא יהא סדק של עיניהם ארוך כשלנו ויכנס בו החול. וכן רגליהם של אפרקיים רחבות — שלא יטבעו בבצעי המים. ורבותינו מפרשים: שדרים בין בצעי המים והולכין יחפין, ומתפשטין רגליהן, לפי שהמנעל דוחק הרגל ומעמידו על דפוס שלו:
Rashi on Shabbat 31a:2:2.english: Because they live among the sands - And the wind blows and enters their eyes. But in another place, [the Gemara] explains: "Terutot" — an expression [meaning that] their sockets are round. And here too I say so: that because they live among the sands, the Omnipresent altered them, so that the slit of their eyes would not be long like ours, [lest] sand enter it. And likewise, [the reason why] the feet of Africans are wide [is] so that they do not sink in marshy waters. But our Rabbis explain: Because they live among marshy waters and walk barefoot, their feet spread out, since footwear compresses the foot and holds it to its mold.

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:4:1.english: Hillel is worthy - [He is] worthy of this.

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:5:1.hebrew: הוציאו בנזיפה - דתניא: הבא לקבל דברי חברות חוץ מדבר אחד, וכן גר הבא להתגייר וקבל עליו דברי תורה חוץ מדבר אחד — אין מקבלין אותו, במסכת בכורות (דף ל:):
Rashi on Shabbat 31a:5:1.english: Cast him out with reprimand - For it is taught [in a baraita]: One who comes to accept the obligations of fellowship [chaverut] except for one matter, and similarly, a convert who comes to convert and accepts upon himself the words of the Torah except for one matter — they do not accept him, in tractate Bekhorot (daf 30b).

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:5:2.hebrew: גייריה - וסמך על חכמתו, שסופו שירגילנו לקבל עליו. דלא דמיא הא ל"חוץ מדבר אחד" — שלא היה כופר בתורה שבעל פה, אלא שלא היה מאמין שהיא מפי הגבורה; והלל הובטח שאחר שילמדנו יסמוך עליו:
Rashi on Shabbat 31a:5:2.english: He converted him - And he relied on his wisdom that in the end he would accustom him to accept [it] upon himself. For this is not similar to [the case of] "except for one matter" — as he did not deny the Oral Torah, but rather did not believe that it was from the mouth of the Almighty; and Hillel was confident that after he taught him, he would rely upon him.

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:5:3.english: He reversed [it] for him - Such as tashrak [i.e., tav, shin, resh, kuf].

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:5:4.hebrew: לאו עלי קא סמכת - מנין אתה יודע שזו אלף וזו בית? אלא שלמדתיך וסמכת עלי. דעל פה נמי, סמוך על דברי:
Rashi on Shabbat 31a:5:4.english: Didn’t you rely on me - From where do you know that this is an alef and this is a bet? Rather, [it is] because I taught you and you relied on me. [Regarding] the Oral [Torah] as well, rely on my words.

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:6:1.hebrew: אמת הבנין - מקל שהוא אמת אורך, ומודדים בו אורך הבנין, שהיו קוצצין עם האומנין כך וכך אמות בכך וכך דמים:
Rashi on Shabbat 31a:6:1.english: The builder's cubit - A stick that is a cubit in length, with which they measure the length of the building, as they would contract with the craftsmen: so many cubits for such and such a price.

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:6:2.hebrew: דעלך סני לחברך לא תעביד - "ריעך וריע אביך אל תעזוב" (משלי כז) — זה הקב"ה; אל תעבור על דבריו, שהרי עליך שנאוי שיעבור חבירך על דבריך. ל"א: חבירך ממש, כגון גזלה, גנבה, ניאוף, ורוב המצות:
Rashi on Shabbat 31a:6:2.english: That which is hateful to you, do not do to your fellow - “Your friend and your father’s friend do not forsake” (Proverbs 27:10) — this is the Holy One, blessed be He; do not transgress His words, for it is hateful to you that your fellow should transgress your words. Another explanation: Your fellow literally — such as robbery, theft, adultery, and most of the commandments.

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:6:3.english: The rest - The rest of the words of the Torah.

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:6:4.hebrew: פירושה - דהא מילתא הוא, לדעת איזה דבר שנאוי. זיל גמור ותדע:
Rashi on Shabbat 31a:6:4.english: Its interpretation - [It is the explanation] of this matter, to know which thing is hateful. Go study, and you will know.

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:7:1.english: A scribe - A teacher of children.

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:8:1.english: Protocols - Arrangements for the needs of the king in keeping with the honor due him.

Rashi on Shabbat 31a:9:1.english: The three of them - These converts.

Tosafot on Shabbat 31a:10:1.hebrew: אמונת זה סדר זרעים - מפרש בירושלמי: שמאמין בחי העולמים וזורע:
Tosafot on Shabbat 31a:10:1.english: "Faith; that is the order of Zera'im" - [It] is explained in the Yerushalmi: That one has faith in the Life of the Worlds and sows.

Tosafot on Shabbat 31a:1:1.english: Who wagered with each other - The laws of asmakhta [a conditional commitment] are explained in another place (Bava Metzia 74a and there).
